label: A judgment of one diagnosis by Claude as a judge (klaxon.judge): a model's, not a rule's or a person's. It saw the right answer and the remedy of the system the diagnosis was made on, and the whole diagnosis; never which model wrote it, nor the rule's verdict. A recorded response, in judge-recording.jsonl.

right_answer.cause: The ledger consumer books a second time every webhook the provider sends again: its dedupe is gone (fault 1's recorded cause, which a deploy brought). Docker did not answer the two tools that read it, so the deploy list and the containers' health could not be read: a right diagnosis says what it could not check, and claims no deploy it has no evidence for. Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.
right_answer.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to the idempotent handler, then repair each double posting with a reversal (a write, so it needs approval)

judgment.why: It correctly places the fault in ledger-consumer: it double-posts the redelivered evt_000272 because there is no event_id dedupe check, and it says it could not check deploys without claiming one; the fix includes rolling ledger-consumer back and reversing the duplicate with approval.
